prompt:
Reference image 1 shows the chosen design of Power capsules. Keep the referenced design exactly — silhouette, proportions, colour palette, materials and rendering style — and show it in the new composition described below (framing and background follow the description, not the reference): SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, widescreen 16:9 side-scrolling arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; gameplay moment illustration. In the thick of a horizontal shoot-'er-up, three power capsules have just popped from a destroyed enemy at the right side of the screen and are drifting leftward through a lattice of hostile fire: a red capsule leading, gold and blue trailing slightly behind, each retaining its glossy pill silhouette, chrome end-caps and inner glowing core, each trailing a short comet-line of its own color to show its drift vector. The bullets around them are classic arcade threats — bright-cored pink, red and violet orbs with dark rims — arranged in curved streams that part around the capsules' path, so the eye reads a safe lane through the fire. At the far left edge, the nose and cyan canopy of a small steel-blue fighter just enter frame, angling up toward the nearest capsule, its orange engine flare streaking behind. The deep-navy space background carries sparse star dust and a faint violet nebula veil. The capsules are lit slightly brighter than everything except bullet cores — they are the prize in the picture. Hover-glow halos, thick dark outlines, saturated arcade palette, lifted deep-navy background, never pure black. No text, no letters, no score UI. Darks stay a lifted deep navy, never pure black; no letterbox bars, no frame or border around the picture. Enemy bullets are round glowing orbs with bright cores and dark rims. No text, letters, numbers, labels, UI or watermark anywhere.
 Reference image 2 shows the small fighter at the left edge: draw it in that design, nose pointing right toward the capsules, its orange engine flame trailing out of its tail to the left; nothing comes out of its nose. The navy starfield fills the whole canvas from the very top edge to the very bottom edge: no black bands above or below the scene.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, explosions destroying capsules, capsules on ground, text, HUD, health bars, watermark, blurry, capsules glowing white, bullets passing through capsules, vertical shooter layout, pure black background
